about: Leans and rules for the tiers, each under forward test. Evidence policy (2026-11-09): a LEAN (40+ decision pairs, 80%+ of slate resamples one way) is ADOPTED, used as a tiebreak or default, only if it holds in both windows, was listed as a candidate before testing, or hit the RULE numbers (80+ pairs, a 90% range clear of zero) and waits on its check (14 slates: 9 to choose on, 5 to check, plus the drop-one-player test); every other lean is a CANDIDATE, forward-tested only. At step 4 chance alone would give about 27 leans of the 67 testable cells; 30 appeared. Anything adopted is dropped if it flips direction over its 14 forward nights. Sources: analysis/nba/report/tier_grade.md, q_lane.md, scripts/nba_take_types.py.
money_policy: 2026-11-09: everything adopted or kept here, switches and leans alike, is PROVISIONAL until its MONEY verdict (top finishes and dollars, written by the contest side into decision_register.csv, column money_verdict, row named by each entry's register field) is in, and may be changed by it. Points and money: both positive, keep. Points positive and money pending, keep provisionally. They disagree: money wins only if its evidence clears its own bar; a decision that loses points is kept only if money clears its bar. The money bar (2026-11-09, the contest side uses the same): MONEY LEAN = at least 80% of slate resamples in the same direction on top-10% lift or average finish percentile, with enough teams in the cell; MONEY RULE = a 90% range above zero on the same reader, same direction in the check slates. Money clears its bar at MONEY LEAN or better; to overturn a points RULE, money must reach MONEY RULE. The contest side's verdicts say LEAN or RULE and the reader they rest on. Both negative, drop. A proposal from the contest side is checked for its points cost on the same decision pairs and its shadow record, and both are shown to the user before anything changes.
